pharm: Inhibits voltage-gated sodium channels and stabilizes neuronal membranes, suppressing release of excitatory neurotransmitters (e.g., glutamate) to control seizures and stabilize mood.
quick: Use if benefit outweighs risk; levels fall in pregnancy
Reduce maintenance dose in significant impairment
Skin for rash, mood/suicidality, drug interactions
summary: Lamotrigine is a phenyltriazine antiepileptic used as adjunctive and (>=16 years) monotherapy for partial-onset and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures and generalized seizures of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and for maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder. It carries a boxed warning for serious, potentially life-threatening rashes including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, which is reduced by strict slow titration. Dosing depends heavily on concomitant drugs (valproate doubles levels; enzyme inducers and estrogen-containing contraceptives lower them).
indications: Adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures in patients aged 2 years and older
Adjunctive therapy for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures (aged 2 and older)
Adjunctive therapy for generalized seizures of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (aged 2 and older)
Conversion to monotherapy in patients aged 16 and older with partial-onset seizures receiving carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone, or valproate
Maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder to delay mood episodes in adults

dosage.d: 25 mg every other day x2 wk, then 25 mg daily x2 wk, then increase by 25-50 mg/day every 1-2 wk
dosage.n: Maintenance 100-200 mg/day (100 mg/day if also on inducers)

dosage.d: 50 mg daily x2 wk, then 100 mg/day x2 wk, then increase by 100 mg/day every 1-2 wk
25 mg daily x2 wk, then 50 mg/day x2 wk, then increase by 50 mg/day every 1-2 wk
25 mg daily x2 wk, 50 mg/day x2 wk, 100 mg/day x1 wk, then 200 mg/day target
dosage.n: Target 200 mg/day; adjust with interacting drugs

dosage.d: Taper over at least 2 weeks (~50% dose reduction per week)
dosage.n: Avoid abrupt withdrawal; do not restart after rash unless benefit clearly outweighs risk

admin: Follow the recommended initial dose and titration exactly to reduce rash risk
Take with or without food; chewable/dispersible and orally disintegrating forms have specific instructions
Use titration kits for the first 5 weeks where provided
Adjust dose when starting/stopping valproate, enzyme inducers, or estrogen-containing contraceptives
Taper over at least 2 weeks when discontinuing
moa: Lamotrigine is thought to act primarily by blocking voltage-sensitive sodium channels, stabilizing presynaptic neuronal membranes and inhibiting the release of excitatory neurotransmitters, particularly glutamate. This reduces sustained repetitive firing and pathologic neuronal excitability underlying seizures and may contribute to its mood-stabilizing effects in bipolar disorder.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to lamotrigine or any formulation component
relative: Concomitant valproate (markedly raises levels - use lower titration)

preg: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. Lamotrigine plasma concentrations can fall substantially during pregnancy (increased clearance), requiring dose adjustment and close monitoring; enroll patients in the pregnancy registry where available.
lact: Lamotrigine is excreted in human milk in clinically relevant amounts; if used during breastfeeding, monitor the infant for rash, apnea, drowsiness, and poor feeding.
renal: Lamotrigine and its glucuronide metabolite are renally eliminated; reduced maintenance doses may be needed in significant renal impairment, and accumulation of the metabolite can occur. Use with caution and monitor.
hepatic: Reduce initial, escalation, and maintenance doses by approximately 25% in moderate to severe hepatic impairment without ascites, and by about 50% with ascites; titrate per clinical response.

major: Valproate - inhibits lamotrigine glucuronidation, roughly doubling levels and greatly increasing rash risk (use reduced doses)
Enzyme-inducing antiepileptics (carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone) and rifampin - lower lamotrigine levels (higher doses needed)
Estrogen-containing oral contraceptives - lower lamotrigine levels; levels rise during the pill-free week
minor: Lamotrigine has weak effects on other drugs' metabolism
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive central nervous system effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive urine drug screen for phencyclidine (PCP) on some immunoassays.

serious: Serious rash (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)
emergency: SJS/TEN with skin blistering and mucosal involvement
DRESS or HLH with fever and organ dysfunction

monitoring: Skin and mucous membranes for rash, especially in first 8 weeks
Mood changes and emergence of suicidal thoughts
Drug levels when interacting drugs change
Cardiac evaluation in patients with structural/ischemic heart disease
counsel: Report any rash, fever, swollen glands, mouth sores, or flu-like symptoms immediately - skin reactions can be life-threatening
Follow the slow dose increases exactly; do not increase faster than instructed
Do not stop suddenly; tapering is needed to avoid seizures
Tell your doctor before starting/stopping birth control pills or valproate, as your dose may need changing
Watch for new or worsening depression, anxiety, or thoughts of self-harm
pk: Therapeutic effect over weeks of titration
~25-33 h alone; ~70 h with valproate; ~12-14 h with inducers
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C; protect from light
pearls: Boxed warning: serious, potentially fatal rashes (including SJS) - higher with rapid titration, high starting dose, or concomitant valproate
Valproate doubles lamotrigine levels (halve doses); enzyme inducers and estrogen-containing contraceptives lower them
Lamotrigine levels drop during pregnancy and rise postpartum - adjust accordingly
Generally weight-neutral and non-sedating; favored bipolar maintenance for depressive episodes
Do not restart after a lamotrigine-related rash unless benefit clearly outweighs risk
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up. If several days are missed, do not resume the previous dose - contact your prescriber, as re-titration may be needed.
overdose: Overdose can cause ataxia, nystagmus, drowsiness, seizures, decreased level of consciousness or coma, QRS widening and cardiac conduction abnormalities, and death. There is no specific antidote; treat with supportive care, airway protection, activated charcoal if appropriate, and cardiac and neurologic monitoring; hemodialysis may remove some drug.
